title: Flatness modulo a directed union of ideals descends to one quotient
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$. Suppose $B$ is a localization of a finitely presented $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and let $P$ be a finitely presented $B$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Let $(J_\lambda)_{\lambda\in L}$ be a nonempty family of ideals of $A$ indexed by a set, directed under inclusion, with $J_\lambda\subseteq\mathfrak m$, and put $J=\bigcup_{\lambda\in L}J_\lambda$. If $P/JP$ is flat over $A/J$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $P/J_\lambda P$ is flat over $A/J_\lambda$ for some $\lambda\in L$. Here $KP$ denotes the submodule consisting of finite sums of products $ax$ with $a\in K$ and $x\in P$. No henselian or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05MN (lemma-flat-at-point), part (2), with A_lambda=A/J_lambda, and Tag 05MK (situation-flat-at-point); underlying general result: more-algebra.tex Tag 05LT (lemma-limit-preserving-flat-at-primes). For quotient local bases, the test set of primes consists only of the maximal ideal of B/J_lambda B.

proof.text: Choose a finitely presented $A$-algebra $C$ and a multiplicative subset $S\subset C$ with $B=S^{-1}C$. Choose a finite presentation $B^u\xrightarrow{H}B^v\to P\to0$. A common denominator for the finitely many entries of $H$ gives $s\in S$ and a matrix $K$ over $C$ with $H=K/s$. Put $N=\operatorname{coker}(K:C^u\to C^v)$. Exact localization identifies $S^{-1}N$ with $\operatorname{coker}K_B$; multiplication by the unit $s$ does not change the image of the presentation matrix, so $S^{-1}N\cong P$. Thus $N$ is finitely presented over $C$. This is the explicit matrix construction of Tag 05N5, with zero quotient ideal, not an invocation of an unstated spreading theorem.

source.place: Tag 05N5 (lemma-construct-fp-module), part (2), clearing the finite presentation matrix; Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact)

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak n$ be the maximal ideal of $B$ and $\mathfrak p$ its inverse image in $C$. Since $B$ is local, each element of $C\setminus\mathfrak p$ becomes a unit in $B$, and $S\subset C\setminus\mathfrak p$. The universal maps $C_{\mathfrak p}\rightleftarrows S^{-1}C=B$ are inverse, as both fix $C$ and the inverses of its inverted elements. Locality of $A\to B$ gives $JC\subset\mathfrak p$, since $J\subset\mathfrak m$. Write $R=A/J$, $\overline C=C/JC$, $\overline N=N/JN$, and $\overline{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak p/JC$. The same fraction maps give $(\overline C)_{\overline{\mathfrak p}}\cong B/JB$ and $(\overline N)_{\overline{\mathfrak p}}\cong P/JP$: the inverse sends the class of $n/t$ to $(n+JN)/(t+JC)$, and a fraction vanishes exactly when a denominator multiple of its numerator lies in the extended ideal or submodule. Consequently $(\overline N)_{\overline{\mathfrak p}}$ is flat over $R$ by hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 05LT (lemma-limit-preserving-flat-at-primes), essentially finitely presented case; specialization of flat.tex Tags 05MK and 05MN to quotient local bases

proof.text: Reducing the finitely many algebra relations of $C$ and the matrix $K$ modulo $J$ shows that $\overline C$ is finitely presented over $R$ and $\overline N$ is finitely presented over $\overline C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-openness-of-flatness], the locus $U=\{Q\in\operatorname{Spec}\overline C:(\overline N)_Q\text{ is flat over }R\}$ is open. Step 2 places $\overline{\mathfrak p}$ in $U$. Write the closed complement as $V(I)$; since $I\not\subseteq\overline{\mathfrak p}$, choose $\overline h\in I\setminus\overline{\mathfrak p}$, which gives $D(\overline h)\subset U$. Lift $\overline h$ to $h\in C\setminus\mathfrak p$. By the prime contraction assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-by-prime], every maximal localization of $(\overline N)_{\overline h}$ over $(\overline C)_{\overline h}$ is a localization $(\overline N)_Q$ with $\overline h\notin Q$, hence is flat over $R$. Apply [lem-sfb-base-flatness-maximal-localizations] with coefficient algebra $(\overline C)_{\overline h}$ to conclude that $(\overline N)_{\overline h}$ is flat over $R$.

source.place: Tag 05LT (lemma-limit-preserving-flat-at-primes), the flat open and principal neighbourhood; algebra.tex Tag 00RC (theorem-openness-flatness) and Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), part (7)

proof.text: Put $D=C[1/h]$ and $E=N[1/h]$. The algebra $D$ is finitely presented over $A$: to a finite presentation of $C$, adjoin one variable $t$ and the single relation $ht-1$. Localizing the matrix $K$ presents $E$ over $D$. For each index $i$ write $R_i=A/J_i$, $D_i=D/J_iD$, and $E_i=E/J_iE$. Quotient scalar extension is given by $(a+J_i)\otimes x\mapsto ax+J_iE$, with inverse $x+J_iE\mapsto1\otimes x$; the same formula works for $D_i$ and for $J$ in place of $J_i$. These maps and the fraction formula $(n/h^r)+JE\mapsto(n+JN)/\overline h^r$ identify $D\otimes_A R$ with $(\overline C)_{\overline h}$ and $E\otimes_A R$ with $(\overline N)_{\overline h}$. In particular the latter module is $R$-flat by step 3.

source.place: Tag 05N5 (lemma-construct-fp-module), presentation calculation; Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat), part (3), construction of the fixed finitely presented model

proof.text: Order the indices by $i\le j$ when $J_i\subseteq J_j$ (a directed preorder; alternatively use the set of distinct ideals). The quotient maps form a directed system with colimit $R=A/J$: a compatible family of maps out of the $R_i$ is a map out of $A$ killing every $J_i$, equivalently killing their union $J$. Fix $i_0$, and restrict to $i\ge i_0$; this tail is cofinal because every index has an upper bound with $i_0$, and its ideals still have union $J$. Apply [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-descent] to this ring system with initial coefficient algebra $A_{i_0}=R_{i_0}$, second algebra $B_{i_0}=D_{i_0}$, and module $N_{i_0}=E_{i_0}$. The first algebra has its zero-generator presentation; the finite presentations of the other two are the relations and matrix of step 4 reduced modulo $J_{i_0}$. The quotient tensor maps of step 4 identify the later algebras and modules with $R_i,D_i,E_i$, and the limit with $R,D\otimes_AR,E\otimes_AR$. Step 4 supplies limit flatness. Hence for some $j\ge i_0$, the module $E_j$ is flat over $R_j$.

source.place: Tag 05LT (lemma-limit-preserving-flat-at-primes), application of algebra.tex Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat), part (3), on the chosen principal neighbourhood

proof.text: Since $h\notin\mathfrak p$, its image is a unit in $B$. Thus $B/J_jB$ is a localization of $D_j$, obtained by further inverting the image of $S$, and the fraction maps of steps 1, 2, and 4 identify the localization of $E_j$ with $P/J_jP$. To check preservation of $R_j$-flatness, tensor an injection $U\hookrightarrow V$ of $R_j$-modules with $E_j$. It stays injective by step 5. Localize this map over $D_j$; exact localization preserves its injectivity. The maps $u\otimes(e/s)\mapsto(u\otimes e)/s$ and $(u\otimes e)/s\mapsto u\otimes(e/s)$ identify its source and target with $U\otimes_{R_j}(P/J_jP)$ and $V\otimes_{R_j}(P/J_jP)$, respectively, and intertwine the maps. Therefore tensoring with $P/J_jP$ preserves every injection, which is exactly flatness over $A/J_j$.

source.place: Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact) and Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), localization and relative flatness; final passage back to the local algebra in more-algebra.tex Tag 05LT
